findings.issue: Remote deletion is not conditional on the ref still being at the SHA that was found merged. If someone pushes new commits to origin/doit/X between the script's `git fetch --prune` and `git push origin --delete doit/X`, those unmerged commits are deleted from origin.
findings.evidence: network (another pusher to origin) -> fetch at line 67 snapshots refs -> for-each-ref --merged selects doit/X -> push --delete at line 116 removes whatever doit/X points to now. In practice the repo has one user and the window is milliseconds, so this is not realistically reachable. The local copy of the commits (if any) remains.
findings.fix: Optional: capture %(objectname) along with the name and delete with a lease, e.g. `git push --force-with-lease=doit/X:<sha> origin :doit/X` (or `--atomic` with per-ref leases), so a moved ref is rejected rather than deleted.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. The prune script passes git-ref-derived branch names as spawnSync argument-array elements (no shell), and they are always prefixed `doit/`, so they cannot be read as options or select main. Deletion only happens with --apply; any other argument fails closed with exit 2; missing main/origin/main or a failed fetch aborts before any deletion. Local deletion uses -D only for refs that for-each-ref --merged reports as merged into main, and the checked-out branch is excluded (git itself refuses branches checked out in other worktrees). The acceptance tests run in mkdtemp with all GIT_* env vars stripped, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, so they cannot reach the real repo. dependabot.yml adds no secrets. Dependabot PRs trigger the existing `pull_request` workflow (not pull_request_target), which has `permissions: contents: read` and uses no secrets, and npm updates still go through the audit gates. The README branch-protection command is documentation only, and enforce_admins:false is a deliberate choice (Q-1). No new dependencies. One MINOR: a TOCTOU race on remote deletion with no lease.
